starter:
# y = x correlated with w, same size: y[i] = x[i-1]*w[0] + x[i]*w[1] + x[i+1]*w[2], zeros outside x
%xb = buffer 6 dtype=f32 slot=0
%wb = buffer 3 dtype=f32 slot=1
%yb = buffer 6 dtype=f32 slot=2
%x  = load %xb
%w  = load %wb
%p  = pad %x pads=[2 0]
%s0 = shrink %p 0 shape=[6]
%s1 = shrink %p 1 shape=[6]
%s2 = shrink %p 2 shape=[6]
%win = stack %s0 %s1 %s2
%w2 = reshape %w shape=[3 1]
%wx = expand %w2 shape=[3 6]
%pr = mul %win %wx
%y  = reduce %pr op=add pop=1
%st = store %yb %y
%y1 = after %yb %st
hints: Each output y[i] needs three neighbours: x[i-1], x[i], x[i+1]. Missing neighbours count as zero.
Pad x by one zero on each side (`pads=[1 1]`), then take three length-6 windows with `shrink` at offsets 0, 1 and 2.
Stack the windows into `[3 6]`, expand w from `[3 1]` to `[3 6]`, multiply, and `reduce pop=1` adds the three taps.
explain: Padding makes every window full size, so one shape covers the edges too. The stack of shifted windows is the im2col view: after it, a convolution is a multiply and a reduce over the tap axis.
title: A same-size conv1d
